newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada building permits rise 8.5 pct in January.
newsitem.headline: Canada building permits rise 8.5 pct in January.

text.p: The value of Canadian building permits issued in January rose 8.5 percent to C$2.413 billion, seasonally adjusted, from December, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
Jan Month pct chg Yr pct change
Economists surveyed by Reuters had forecast on average a month-on-month rise of 5.0 percent after a 4.6 percent decline in December.
Statistics Canada said building permits rose in January in the wake of low mortgage rates and stronger demand for new and existing homes.

Ontario led the resurgence in the housing sector, with the value or residential permits rising 25.1 percent on the strength of a sharp increase in the value of permits for both single and multi-family components, the agency said.

It said the value of plans for single-family dwellings rose 15.0 percent to C$1.2 billion in January, the highest level since November 1991. Multi-family construction intentions fell 1.0 percent to C$392 million, the second drop in a row.

And overal housing market activity continued to show higher activity since the beginning of 1996. The January resale housing market was 51.2 percent stronger than the same period a year earlier, Statscan said.
Building permits are an early indicator of future demand for labour and material by construction and contruction- related industries.
According to the Canada Mortgage and Housing Corporation, about 95 percent of the residential building permits issued translate into actual housing starts.
